title: ZTIE dashboard JSON payload contract (v1)
description: The bounded, DERIVED DASHBOARD JSON PAYLOAD assembled by the Story 4.2 Hub-side dashboard orchestrator (RD-042) — the Phase-4 DATA LAYER the real-time dashboard (4.3 render) consumes. It comes in ONE of two shapes, discriminated by `view`: a PER-INTAKE DETAIL (view=`intake`) that REUSES the Story 4.1 status read-model (`status.contract.v1`) as its core + adds a normalized `threat` color band + an `action` block for the human APPROVE/REJECT control; or a FLEET/LIST (view=`fleet`) of recent intakes read from the tracking table's `status-received_at-index` GSI (bounded, newest-first, NO full scan) + a `metrics` block of tracking-native counts and (stubbed) operational health. It is an ON-DEMAND DERIVED TRANSPORT SHAPE, NOT a durable stored record: 4.2 is a READ/transform behind an orchestrator Lambda, it adds NO durable tracking field and does NOT hang off the tracking-table stream. It is READ/transform only — it does NOT re-normalize / re-correlate / re-score / rebuild findings / re-derive the verdict (3.1-3.5, done) and makes NO model call (no Bedrock client, no Bedrock grant); the ONLY new derivation is the display `threat_tier` (from the combined score / highest gap severity / contradiction), a color band NEVER a verdict. It is Hub-SIDE only (RD-009): it reasons ONLY over the derived Hub-side fields, NEVER the raw payload / findings text / raw trace (which never leave Forensic), and it never crosses the RD-013 gate. CRUCIALLY (RD-040), the 3.5 recommendation it surfaces is ADVISORY and NEVER acted upon: nothing routes / promotes / destroys / moves an artifact on it; the enforcement decision is a HUMAN actively selecting PASS or FAIL at the Phase-4 gate (4.4/4.6/4.7). Every payload surfaces the recommendation ALONGSIDE the human `decision`, whose only value 4.2 can report is `pending`; the advisory field is named `recommended_verdict` (NOT a bare `verdict`), and there is deliberately NO bare `verdict` / `safe` / `approved` / `forward` / `pass_fail` / `malicious` / `clean` field. Allow-list: additionalProperties false at every level; every field typed and enum/length/range-bounded; every array maxItems-capped (the fleet list default 50, hard max 100). DERIVED-ONLY. OWN version pin (DASHBOARD_CONTRACT_VERSION).

contract_version.description: Dashboard payload schema version. Pinned SEPARATELY on the 4.2 Lambda (DASHBOARD_CONTRACT_VERSION) so this shape versions independently of every stored-record contract's pin and of the 4.1 status read-model pin.

view.description: Which payload shape this is: `intake` (per-intake detail) or `fleet` (recent-intakes list + metrics). A single discriminator so the render branches without guessing.

assembled_at.description: RFC3339/ISO-8601 UTC timestamp (Z-suffixed) the 4.2 Lambda ASSEMBLED this payload in the Hub. A payload assembly time, not a pipeline event time.

intake.description: PER-INTAKE DETAIL (present iff view=`intake`). The 4.1 status read-model (`status.contract.v1`) as `status` + a normalized `threat` color band + an `action` block for the human APPROVE/REJECT control.

status.description: The full Story 4.1 per-intake status read-model, reused verbatim (status.contract.v1). 4.2 does NOT re-assemble it; it embeds 4.1's output as-is. `true` here means: validated separately by the status contract; this contract does not re-declare its internals (see status.contract.v1.json).

threat.description: The normalized THREAT TIER the dashboard renders as a color band (dark-theme, graduated low/medium/high/critical — the stakeholder requirement), plus the already-derived evidence it was banded from. A DISPLAY band derived from the combined 3.3 score / the highest 3.4 gap severity / the contradiction flag — NEVER a verdict, NEVER acted upon.

tier.description: The color band (unknown / low / medium / high / critical). `unknown` when there is not enough derived evidence yet to band. A display band, never a verdict.

combined_score.description: The combined 3.3 risk score (0-100) the tier was primarily banded from, echoed as context. Present only when a combined score is available. EVIDENCE, never a verdict.

highest_gap_severity.description: The worst 3.4 gap severity considered when banding, echoed as context.

contradiction_present.description: True iff a contradiction finding was present (the lanes disagree), which raises the display tier. A descriptive fact, never a verdict.

action.description: The data the dashboard's human APPROVE/REJECT control keys on (RD-040): the intake identity the 4.4/4.6/4.7 routing action targets + the ADVISORY 3.5 recommendation + the PENDING human decision. 4.2 NEVER acts on this — it is the control's input, not an executed decision. `decision` is `pending` (4.2 never reports a made decision); the advisory field is `recommended_verdict` (never a bare `verdict`).

intake_id.description: The intake UUIDv4 the human accept/reject action targets (the key the Phase-4 routing 4.4/4.6/4.7 uses).

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the raw artifact body (integrity key bound to intake_id) so the human action targets exactly this artifact.

recommendation_status.description: The 3.5 recommendation status carried through (recommended / no_scores / incomplete / not_yet_recommended). HONEST production status, never a verdict.

recommended_verdict.description: The 3.5 ADVISORY recommended verdict (PASS / FAIL / INCONCLUSIVE), surfaced for the human to triage. NEVER acted upon automatically. Present ONLY when a 3.5 recommendation has landed.

decision.description: The human accept/reject decision marker. ALWAYS `pending` — 4.2 NEVER reports a made decision; the human's actual selection is a SEPARATE, human-owned Phase-4 field 4.2 does not echo. Enumerated to exactly one value so this payload can never assert a made decision.

advisory.description: Always true: an explicit machine-readable flag that the recommended_verdict is ADVISORY and must NEVER be acted upon automatically. Defense-in-depth so the render cannot treat the recommendation as an effective decision.

fleet.description: FLEET/LIST view (present iff view=`fleet`): a bounded, newest-first list of recent intakes + roll-up counts + operational health. Read from the `status-received_at-index` GSI (NO full scan).

intakes.description: The bounded, newest-first list of recent-intake rows (default 50, hard max 100).

items.description: One recent intake summarized for the fleet/list view: identity + how far it got + its color band + the advisory recommendation + the pending human decision. A compact row; the render fetches full per-intake detail on demand.

intake_id.description: The intake UUIDv4 (the tracking-record key + row identity).

sha256.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the raw artifact (integrity key), when present on the item.

status.description: The tracking record's lifecycle status string (e.g. RECEIVED), echoed for the row. Bounded, inert; NOT a verdict.

received_at.description: The intake's received_at timestamp, echoed so the render can sort/label the timeline.

overall_stage.description: The furthest pipeline stage reached, HONESTLY reported. NOT a verdict.

threat_tier.description: The normalized color band for the row (display, never a verdict).

recommended_verdict.description: The 3.5 ADVISORY recommended verdict (PASS / FAIL / INCONCLUSIVE), when one has landed. NEVER acted upon.

decision.description: The human accept/reject decision marker for the row. ALWAYS `pending`.

returned_count.description: How many rows this payload actually returned (<= the cap).

truncated.description: True iff more recent intakes existed than the cap returned (the render can show a 'showing N of many' hint). A bounded-output fact.

metrics.description: Roll-up metrics for the returned window. The pipeline counts are DERIVED from the returned rows (tracking-native); the operational health blocks (AMI build / sensor / cost) are STUBBED `not_wired` — their real data sources are deferred to a follow-on story, with the SHAPE fixed here so the render never changes.

window_count.description: Total intakes summarized in this metrics window (== returned_count).

by_stage.description: Count of returned intakes at each `overall_stage`. Fixed, allow-listed keys.

received.description: Intakes whose furthest stage is received.

classified.description: Intakes whose furthest stage is classified.

collected.description: Intakes whose furthest stage is collected.

correlated.description: Intakes whose furthest stage is correlated.

scored.description: Intakes whose furthest stage is scored.

assessed.description: Intakes whose furthest stage is assessed.

recommended.description: Intakes whose furthest stage is recommended.

by_recommended_verdict.description: Count of returned intakes by the ADVISORY 3.5 recommended_verdict (context; NEVER an acted-upon tally). `none` = no recommendation landed yet.

none.description: Intakes with no recommendation landed yet.

by_threat_tier.description: Count of returned intakes by normalized display `threat_tier`. For the dashboard's color roll-up.

unknown.description: Intakes in the unknown color band.

low.description: Intakes in the low color band.

medium.description: Intakes in the medium color band.

high.description: Intakes in the high color band.

critical.description: Intakes in the critical color band.

ami_build_health.description: An operational health block: a status + an optional bounded, inert detail note. For metrics whose real data source is deferred to a follow-on story (AMI build health / sensor status / cost), status is `not_wired` — an explicit placeholder so the render's shape is stable and the source can be wired later with no render change.

status.description: ok / degraded / unavailable / not_wired. `not_wired` = the real data source is deferred (an explicit placeholder, not an error).

detail.description: Optional short, bounded, inert note about the health status. Never a verdict, never raw content.

sensor_status.description: An operational health block: a status + an optional bounded, inert detail note. For metrics whose real data source is deferred to a follow-on story (AMI build health / sensor status / cost), status is `not_wired` — an explicit placeholder so the render's shape is stable and the source can be wired later with no render change.

status.description: ok / degraded / unavailable / not_wired. `not_wired` = the real data source is deferred (an explicit placeholder, not an error).

detail.description: Optional short, bounded, inert note about the health status. Never a verdict, never raw content.

cost.description: An operational health block: a status + an optional bounded, inert detail note. For metrics whose real data source is deferred to a follow-on story (AMI build health / sensor status / cost), status is `not_wired` — an explicit placeholder so the render's shape is stable and the source can be wired later with no render change.

status.description: ok / degraded / unavailable / not_wired. `not_wired` = the real data source is deferred (an explicit placeholder, not an error).

detail.description: Optional short, bounded, inert note about the health status. Never a verdict, never raw content.

dashboard_note.description: Optional short, bounded, non-executable note framing this as a DERIVED read-only dashboard payload whose recommendation is ADVISORY + human-gated. Descriptive, never a verdict.
